_readme: The list of documents the monitor re-reads. This is the file you edit.
Each entry needs a doc_id (any short unique name), the card ids it covers,
a label for humans, and a url.
There is deliberately no 'pdf' or 'html' field. The fetcher works out the
type from the response, because some issuers serve a PDF from a URL that
looks like a web page - ICICI's tnc-for-amazon-pay.page is one.
Set url to null for a document you know exists but have not found a link
for yet. The monitor reports it as not_configured rather than quietly
watching nothing.
Set known_blocked to true when the issuer refuses the document to every
automated client. The monitor still tries it each run, but a failure will
not mark the scheduled job red - otherwise the job would be permanently
failing and you would stop reading it. If a blocked document ever does
come back, the run says so and you can remove the flag.
Three kinds of document are listed here, and they do different jobs:
scope 'notices' - the issuer's own announcements page, where it is
required to publish changes before they take effect.
Best signal there is for a devaluation: it is about
change by definition, it names the affected card, and
it usually carries the effective date. Watch these
first.
scope 'card'    - the specific card's terms. Carries the reward rates
and caps, so it shows what the rate became.
scope 'issuer'  - one MITC covering every card that bank issues. Catches
fee, interest and surcharge changes, but NOT reward
rates - an MITC is an RBI fee disclosure and simply
does not contain per-card earn rates. A card covered
only by an MITC is not protected against devaluation.
EVERY url below was fetched for real on 2026-07-27. Nothing here is
guessed. The notes record what actually happened, including the failures.
_coverage_note: card_ids below include cards that are not yet in assets/rules.json. That is
deliberate: monitoring a document costs nothing extra, and when you do add
a card to the dataset its change history is already there waiting.
Until a card exists in rules.json the app cannot rank it, so a user cannot
own it, so its alerts stay invisible to them. Nothing breaks - the alert is
written and simply never matches an owned card.

card_names.hdfc-diners-black: HDFC Bank Diners Club Black Metal

documents.label: SBI Card customer notices
documents.note: Verified as HTML, 180 KB. The single most useful SBI document. At the time of adding it was announcing, with effective dates, that the Reward Points Programme on two cards would be revised, that statement-credit redemption would be capped at 60,000 points a month, and that redemption would only be possible in multiples of 4,000 points. None of that appears in the MITC.

documents.label: SBI Card revision of charges
documents.note: Verified, 2.0 MB PDF.

documents.label: Cashback SBI Card terms booklet
documents.note: Verified, 1.3 MB PDF. Carries the reward rates and caps.

documents.label: SBI Card Most Important Terms and Conditions
documents.note: Verified, 1.5 MB PDF. This is the copy SBI links from its own tnc.page, so it is the canonical one. A second file english-mitc.pdf also resolves but is only 380 KB and appears to be older.

documents.label: BPCL SBI Card Octane terms and MITC
documents.note: Verified, 3.2 MB PDF.

documents.label: SimplyCLICK SBI Card terms booklet
documents.note: NEEDS URL. SBI does publish per-card booklets - cashback-tnc-booklet.pdf and the BPCL one both resolve - but the SimplyCLICK filename is not linked from tnc.page and guessing at it returned 404. High value: SimplyCLICK is one of SBI's highest-volume cards.

documents.label: SimplySAVE SBI Card terms booklet
documents.note: NEEDS URL. Same situation as SimplyCLICK above.

documents.label: Axis Bank credit card important announcements
documents.note: Verified as HTML, 735 KB. Names individual cards when their terms change - at the time of adding it carried the Flipkart Axis exclusion of utility, insurance and education payments from cashback, and the milestone-spend exclusion of rent and wallet transactions. This is the page that would have caught the April 2026 Axis devaluation.

documents.label: Axis Bank Miles & More card page
documents.note: Verified as HTML, 705 KB. Co-branded with Lufthansa's Miles & More programme, so the award-mile earn rate and any transfer-ratio change would show up here.

documents.label: Axis Bank MAGNUS for Burgundy terms and conditions
documents.note: Verified, 597 KB PDF. Titled 'Revision of ... Terms & Conditions', so the document itself is the change record. Magnus for Burgundy is invite-only for Axis Burgundy clients and was hit by the same 2 April 2026 devaluation as Atlas, though it kept a better 5:4 point-to-mile ratio.

documents.label: Axis Bank ACE terms and conditions
documents.note: Verified. Note the www.axisbank.com copy of this file 404s; the campaign subdomain is the working one.

documents.label: Airtel Axis Bank card terms and conditions
documents.note: Verified, 450 KB PDF. This card was hit by the April 2026 Axis devaluation, so it is worth watching closely.

documents.label: Axis Bank credit cards MITC
documents.note: Verified. Served as a PDF from a URL with no file extension.

documents.label: Flipkart Axis Bank card terms
documents.note: NEEDS URL. The campaign.axisbank.com pattern that works for ACE and Airtel did not resolve for Flipkart. The issuer MITC above does not carry the Flipkart and Myntra reward caps.

documents.label: Axis Bank Atlas terms and transfer partners
documents.note: NEEDS URL. The EDGE Miles transfer partner list is what changes on this card, and it lives on a page we have not located.

documents.label: ICICI Bank credit card MITC
documents.note: Reachable only through the curl fallback in fetch.dart. ICICI returns 403 to Dart's own HTTP client whatever headers it sends, and 200 to curl - the difference is the TLS handshake, not the request.

documents.label: Amazon Pay ICICI card terms
documents.note: Reachable via the curl fallback. Despite the .page ending this returns a PDF, which is why the fetcher sniffs content type instead of trusting the URL.

documents.label: ICICI Bank Coral card page
documents.note: Verified as HTML, 444 KB.

documents.label: ICICI Platinum Chip card page
documents.note: Verified as HTML, 437 KB. This is the product page for the standard Platinum. Note that /platinum-credit-card also returns 200 but is a card-comparison listing rather than this card's own page, so it is not watched.

documents.label: ICICI Emeralde Private Metal card page
documents.note: Verified as HTML, 481 KB.

documents.label: ICICI Emeralde card page
documents.note: Verified as HTML, 468 KB.

documents.label: YES Bank credit cards index
documents.note: NEEDS URL. The page at /personal-banking/yes-individual/cards/credit-cards returns 200 and 300 KB, but every word of it is rendered by JavaScript - the extractor finds no readable text at all. Left unconfigured rather than watched, because a document that can never yield text would fail every run, go stale, and turn the scheduled job permanently red. Reading YES Bank needs a headless browser.

documents.label: YES Bank Marquee card terms
documents.note: NEEDS URL. YES Bank serves documents from a JS-rendered asset API whose content ids rotate; every asset URL found via search returned 404 when fetched, with and without the channelToken query string, and the product page slug 404s too. Open the Marquee page in a browser, copy the terms PDF link, and paste it here.

documents.label: IDFC FIRST Bank notice board
documents.note: Verified as HTML, 1.8 MB. Where IDFC posts changes before they take effect.

documents.label: IDFC FIRST Bank credit card MITC
documents.note: Verified. Large file, around 4 MB.

documents.label: IDFC FIRST credit card documents index
documents.note: Verified, HTML. Useful because new document links appear here first.

documents.label: IDFC FIRST Millennia card page
documents.note: Verified as HTML, 1.8 MB.

documents.label: HDFC Bank MITC document index
documents.note: Reachable, but it is only a list of links to per-language PDFs - 23 lines with no actual terms. Kept because it is how we would notice HDFC republishing or restructuring its MITC. The document with the real content is hdfc-mitc-english below, which is blocked.

documents.label: HDFC Bank credit card MITC (English)
documents.note: BLOCKED. Returns 403 with an HTML error body to Dart, curl and PowerShell alike. This is the document that actually carries HDFC's fees and charges, so until it becomes reachable those need checking by hand. Left in the list because GitHub's runners come from different addresses and may get through.

documents.label: Swiggy HDFC Bank card page
documents.note: Verified as HTML. Carries the 10%/5%/1% rates and the Rs 249 minimum.

documents.label: Tata Neu Infinity HDFC Bank card page
documents.note: Verified as HTML.

documents.label: HDFC Millennia card page
documents.note: Verified as HTML, 1.2 MB, carrying 'Earn 3 Reward points per 200 spent'. Note the slug: /millennia 403s but /millennia-credit-card does not. HDFC's blocking is per-URL, not per-card, so a 403 is worth retrying with a longer slug before concluding a document is unreachable.

documents.label: HDFC Regalia Gold card page
documents.note: Verified as HTML, 1.3 MB, carrying '5 Reward Points on every Rs'. Same slug trap as Millennia above: /regalia-gold 403s, /regalia-gold-credit-card does not.

documents.label: HDFC Diners Club Black Metal Edition card page
documents.note: Verified as HTML, 1.2 MB, carrying the quarterly bonus reward point structure.

documents.label: HDFC Infinia Metal Edition card page
documents.note: Verified as HTML. /infinia 403s; /infinia-credit-card works.

documents.label: HDFC MoneyBack+ card page
documents.note: Verified as HTML.

documents.label: IndianOil HDFC Bank card page
documents.note: Verified as HTML.

documents.label: American Express credit card member agreement
documents.note: Verified, 210 KB PDF. Amex's own spelling of the filename.

documents.label: American Express charge card MITC
documents.note: Verified, 272 KB PDF. Charge cards are a separate product line from the lending cards above.

documents.label: HSBC India credit card MITC
documents.note: Verified, 86 KB PDF.

documents.label: HSBC Visa Cashback card terms
documents.note: Verified, 96 KB PDF.

documents.label: HSBC Smart Value card MITC and tariff
documents.note: Verified, 3.6 MB PDF.

documents.label: OneCard MITC (Federal Bank issued)
documents.note: Verified, 915 KB PDF. OneCard is not a bank - FPL Technologies runs the product and a partner bank issues the card, so there is one MITC per issuing bank rather than one for OneCard.

documents.label: OneCard MITC (CSB Bank issued)
documents.note: Verified, 679 KB PDF.

documents.label: OneCard terms and conditions (CSB Bank)
documents.note: Verified, 516 KB PDF.

documents.label: OneCard MITC (SBM Bank issued)
documents.note: Verified, 1.0 MB PDF.

documents.label: OneCard MITC (IDBI Bank issued)
documents.note: Verified, 1.3 MB PDF. Served from OneCard's own asset host rather than the bank's, so this one may be versioned by filename - if it starts 404ing, look for a new timestamp suffix.

documents.label: Standard Chartered India credit card help pages
documents.note: Verified as HTML, 331 KB. Weak substitute: Standard Chartered does not publish a single MITC PDF that we could find, so this page is the best available signal that something changed.

documents.label: Standard Chartered India form and document centre
documents.note: Verified as HTML, 336 KB. Watched because a new terms document would be linked from here first.

documents.label: American Express India card range
documents.note: Watched so a new card or a withdrawn one shows up. Amex India is a small range, and the MITC PDFs above carry the actual terms.
